newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't suffers reform amendment defeat.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't suffers reform amendment defeat.

text.p: The Brazilian government suffered a first defeat in the Chamber of Deputies Wednesday when it failed to failed to muster enough votes to add an amendment to its civil service reform bill, officials said.
The government needed a three-fifths majority of 308 votes to approve the amendment, which would have relaxed rules on hiring of low-paid public sector workers.
But it managed to gather only 298 votes in favor of the proposed alteration to the text of the reform bill.

As it stands, the bill requires the federal, state and municipal authorities to go through a formal hiring procedure involving examinations and other tests for all employees. The government wanted to relax those rules for unskilled workers.
The lower house was due to continue voting on other amendments Wednesday. The bill was approved for a first time in the lower house earlier this month.

Once the amendments have been approved or rejected, the legislation needs a second approval in the Chamber of Deputies before advancing to the Senate where it also requires two three-fifths majorities.
